newsitem.title: USA: ConEd puts 975 MW NY nuke in cold shutdown.
newsitem.headline: ConEd puts 975 MW NY nuke in cold shutdown.

text.p: Consolidated Edison Co of New York (ConEd) said Monday it put its 975 megawatt Indian Point 2 nuclear generating unit in cold shutdown over the weekend to support work on the non-nuclear side of the plant.

The unit along the Hudson River north of New York City was shut January 27 and held in hot shutdown mode. During the outage, ConEd identified a problem linked to a cleaning material found in the unit's feedwater and condensate systems.
"Plant personnel will continue inspections, identify the extent of the problem and remove the material. A thorough root-cause analysis is ongoing," ConEd said in a statement.
ConEd still has not scheduled a startup date for Indian Point
The utility said it planned to meet with the Nuclear Regulatory Commission (NRC) prior to return to service to discuss the results of its inspections and analyses connected with the shutdown.
A ConEd spokeswoman said the meeting between ConEd and NRC has not been set.
